https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/08/03/szel.text: Menü Kereső Meghalt Szelényi Iván szociológus Belföld Iván-Nagy Szilvia Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom Hosszú betegség után, életének 88. évében meghalt Szelényi Iván szociológus, a Tárki Zrt. igazgatósági tagja – jelentette be a Facebookon Szelényi Iván halálát a Tárki Társadalomkutatási Intézet Zrt. Szelényi Iván Budapesten született 1938-ban. A Yale Egyetem Szociológiai és Politikatudományi Tanszékének William Graham Sumner professzor emeritusa, a New York University Abu Dhabi Társadalomtudományi Tanszékének alapító dékánja és Max Weber professzor emeritusa, aki továbbá az American Academy of Arts and Sciences ösztöndíjasa és a Magyar Tudományos Akadémia rendes tagja volt, valamint a Corvinus Egyetem, a Flinders Egyetem, a Friedrich-Alexander Egyetem, a European University Institute és a Közép-Európai Egyetem díszdoktoraként is jegyezték. Korábban a Magyar Szociológiai Társaság elnöke és az Amerikai Szociológiai Társaság alelnöke is volt. A Kaliforniai Egyetem Luckmann Distinguished Teaching díjban részesítette, a magyar állam Széchenyi-díjjal ismerte el munkásságát. Számos, a magyar társadalommal foglalkozó könyvnek volt szerzője/társszerzője, köztük például Az értelmiség útja az osztályhatalomhoz (1979) címűnek is. A könyv kéziratának külföldre juttatása miatt letartóztatták, és 1975-ben ki is utasították Magyarországról. Innen előbb az angliai Kent Egyetemre ment vendégprofesszornak, majd Ausztráliába költözött, ahol megalapította az adelaide-i Dél-ausztráliai Flinders Egyetem Szociológia Tanszékét és annak első vezető professzora lett. Életrajzi adatai szerint 1981-ben az Amerikai Egyesült Államokba ment, ahol több egyetemen is dolgozott a szociológiai tanszék vezetőjeként. Szelényi Iván jegyezte a Városi társadalmi egyenlőtlenségek (1983), Szocialista vállalkozók (1988), Kapitalisták nélküli kapitalizmus (1998) és A kirekesztettség változó formái (2006) c. műveket is. Szelényi Iván utolsó munkája a Tárki kiadásában jelent meg két kötetben a magyar társadalom utolsó tíz évének alakulásáról. Kedvenceink Partnereinktől Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! https://www.breitbart.com/europe/2026/07.text: KYIV, Ukraine (AP) – A Russian ballistic missile and drone barrage across Ukraine overnight killed at least eight civilians, including children, and injured more than 50 others, officials said Thursday, and NATO scrambled its warplanes after one of the missiles crossed the country’s western border into Poland. The blitz expanded Russia´s almost daily bombardment of Ukrainian cities, including the capital of Kyiv where tens of thousands spent the night sheltering in subway stations, as Moscow apparently looked to exploit Kyiv´s critical shortage of Western-supplied anti-ballistic missile defenses. NATO said a Russian missile entered Polish airspace during the onslaught and landed in a rural area. It caused no injuries or damage but could deepen tensions between the military alliance and Moscow, as wary European countries fear the 4-year-old war could spill into their territory. NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte called it “yet another reckless act by Russia and a dangerous consequence of its war against Ukraine.” Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said it was “a very serious incident,” but added: “There are absolutely no reasons to believe that Poland was the target.” Russia’s barrage struck areas of Ukraine where weapons are believed to be stored and manufactured. Ukrainian long-range drones and missiles have battered Russia’s oil sector, causing a fuel crisis. The attack came two days after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met with U.S. President Donald Trump and representatives of American defense companies as he pleads for swifter and bigger deliveries of Patriot air defense systems to stop Russia´s ballistic missiles. The Iran war has drained stockpiles of the U.S.-made interceptors. Trump has promised to grant Ukraine licenses to build its own Patriots, but production could take many months. “Given the critical shortage of air defense missiles from our partners, our warriors are accomplishing truly incredible things, demonstrating a very high level of professionalism,” Zelenskyy said on social media. “This Russian terror once again proves that protection against the Russian missile threat is the most important task when it comes to saving the lives of our people,” he said. Zelenskyy said at least 10 Ukrainian regions were attacked, with dozens of homes, businesses and infrastructure facilities destroyed or damaged. Russia launched more than 70 missiles, a significant number of them ballistic missiles, he said, and over 280 attack drones, of which more than 260 were intercepted. The Russian Defense Ministry said it targeted Ukrainian air bases, arms factories and military telecommunications and logistics facilities, including drone factories and storage depots, as well as plants for missiles, aircraft repairs, electronics and chemicals. In the Dnipropetrovsk region, the Russian attack killed six people and wounded 10, said Oleksandr Hanzha, head of the regional military administration, in a post on Telegram. Children were among the dead – a 6-year-old girl and boys aged 11 and 17 in the area of Kryvyi Rih, Zelenskyy’s hometown, Hanzha added. The children´s parents were killed in the same attack, but two more children were pulled alive from the rubble, Zelenskyy said. “It was an ordinary home, blown (to) smithereens by a ballistic missile,” he said on X. In Kyiv, Russian forces struck the capital with ballistic missiles, killing a 31-year-old man and wounding two others, the National Police press service said. More than 56,000 people sheltered in Kyiv´s subway stations overnight, according to the Facebook post from the metro system. A cruise missile attack struck the western city of Lviv, killing one person and wounding over 30, including children aged 6, 13 and 15, said Maksym Kozytskyi, head of the Lviv regional military administration. In the Poltava region, a drone hit warehouses, killing one person, said regional military head Vitalii Diakivnych. Russian forces also dropped three powerful glide bombs on an industrial zone in the southern city of Kherson, killing a 56-year-old man, local officials said. A Russian Kh-101 cruise missile crossed into Poland overnight, violating NATO airspace, Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said on X, calling it a clear demonstration that strengthening Ukraine´s air defenses would also guarantee wider European security. Responding to the missile alert, NATO forces in Poland scrambled two fighter jets, an attack helicopter and two other aircraft, and activated ground defenses, said Col. Michael O´Connell, the spokesperson for the alliance´s military command in Belgium. The missile quickly disappeared from radar, the Polish Armed Forces said. A helicopter flew to its last known location, where the crew discovered a probable impact site in a farming area in Lublin province, the command said. Investigators found fragments indicating that the object was a Kh-101 missile, Polish news agency PAP reported. Tusk had met with Zelenskyy in Lublin on Wednesday to discuss defense issues. NATO military commander Gen. Alexus G. Grynkewich told Poland´s Defense Chief Gen. Wieslaw Kukulan the military alliance “will continue to take all necessary measures to defend NATO territory,” O´Donnell said. Meanwhile, Russia´s Defense Ministry said air defenses downed 258 Ukrainian drones overnight. A depot belonging to Wildberries online retailer was set ablaze in Russia’s Penza region southeast of Moscow, in the latest strike on the company’s warehouses, Penza Gov. Oleg Melnichenko. Four people were injured and 200 workers were evacuated, he said, adding that about 100 firefighters were deployed. Wildberries also reported its warehouse in Sarapul in the Udmurtia region more than 1,000 kilometers (600 miles) from Ukraine, was struck by a Ukrainian drone and set ablaze. It said the workers had been safely evacuated. The Russian online news outlet Astra reported that another Wildberries depot in the Perm region in the Urals was also set ablaze by a Ukrainian drone strike. Regional authorities reported a Ukrainian drone attack but didn´t give information about the damage. Thursday´s attacks on Wildberries warehouses brought to 14 the number of the retailer´s depots struck by Ukrainian drones in under two weeks. Ukraine accuses Wildberries of supplying goods that can be used by the Russian military. Ukrainian drone units destroyed four more vessels belonging to Russia´s “shadow fleet” of sanctions-busting tankers, bringing the total to 205 since the operation began July 6, Robert “Madyar” Brovdi, commander of the Unmanned Systems Forces, said on his Telegram channel. https://www.politico.eu/article/ceuta-sp.text: CEUTA, Spain — Spanish police fired shots into the air Monday morning as they worked to clear several thousand young men from an encampment in a parking lot beside Ceuta’s city hospital. The chaotic scene, with officers using batons to direct migrants toward the center of the city, was an uncomfortable reminder of the gap between early assurances from Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and his government that the crisis was largely over — and the reality unfolding in Ceuta’s streets. At the time, Spanish and EU officials said that nearly all of 72,000 migrants who crossed from Morocco to Ceuta had abandoned the city . But as his police was intervening on Monday morning, Sánchez had to concede in a radio interview that around 5,000 of them remained in the Spanish territory. Advertisement Advertisement That number is disputed by officials like Ceuta Mayor-President Juan Jesús Vivas, who maintains that some 10,000 unauthorized people are still in the city. The CEP police union and Spanish National Police officers who spoke to Axel Springer’s Global Reporters Network agreed with the larger figure. Among the migrants that remain in the city are some 1,200 unaccompanied minors who are due to be transferred to shelters on the Iberian Peninsula in the coming weeks, Sánchez said Monday. The prime minister has vowed that his government will resolve the crisis with “dignity” and in accordance with the law. In practice, that means migrants must be allowed to file asylum claims and have their cases considered — a process that could substantially delay any deportations. The unresolved situation is turning Ceuta into a theater of ongoing violence between locals, Spanish authorities and the remaining migrants. Several Spanish soldiers were injured after a group of around 40 young migrants pelted them with stones last week. In a separate incident, police arrested three migrants Sunday accused of throwing Molotov cocktails at a platoon patrolling the exclave. Meanwhile, Spanish police last week intervened to protect migrants after local demonstrators stormed their improvised encampment on Ceuta’s El Trampolín beach and set fire to their belongings . Advertisement Advertisement It’s on El Trampolín that Laarvi and his son Omar, both from Tetouan in Morocco, set up camp. “My son couldn’t find work back home,” Laarvi said. The men said they dream of a better life on the Spanish mainland, and perhaps someday further north in Europe. But those dreams are unlikely to come to fruition. Sánchez confirmed Monday that those who entered Ceuta for economic reasons would not qualify for asylum and would be subject to deportation. Escalating violence The removals cannot come soon enough for locals frustrated with the continued presence of thousands of migrants in the city. Shelters and tents along Tramoplín beach in Ceuta on Aug. 31, 2026. | Antonio Sempere “Normally, elderly people spend the summer at the beach, but they can’t do that anymore,” said Jalid Ali Amar, a local resident who owns a restaurant near the encampment on El Trampolín beach. Ali Amar said the city’s inhabitants had been forced to endure weeks of chaos. He added that he had no respect for the migrants “because they have no respect” for locals, many of whom he said are now too afraid to leave their homes because of the deteriorating security situation. Sebastián Sützl, a spokesperson for Spain’s CEP police union in Madrid, said crime in the exclave had increased eightfold since July 30, but provided no evidence to substantiate the claim. Spain’s interior ministry declined to confirm or deny a rise in criminality, saying it had yet to receive the latest crime statistics from Ceuta. Advertisement Advertisement During a visit to the exclave last week, however, Attorney General Teresa Peramato confirmed that authorities had detected an increase in criminal assaults and crimes against private property over the past month. And on Monday, Ceuta’s Public Prosecutor’s Office said it was investigating 22 alleged sexual assaults targeting migrant women and girls, as well as an additional case involving a man belonging to the LGBTQ+ community. “Many women have been raped,” said Helena Maleno, spokesperson for migrant rights NGO Caminando Fronteras. She added that the true number could be higher than the figure confirmed by Spanish officials, as migrant women may not know how to report sexual assaults or trust authorities enough to do so. Aid groups are increasingly caught in the middle of the violence. Nolte Bauer, an activist with Mission Lifeline, a German NGO that works with migrants and internally displaced people, said he had received death threats. He added that unidentified people had attempted to slash the wheels of his truck, from which migrants can charge their phones for free. Protesters have also tried to stop Red Cross vehicles from distributing food to migrants. “I understand that the current situation is stressful for local residents, and I understand that they are protesting,” Bauer said. “But threatening people with death, hunting people down and setting camps on fire — that crosses a line.” Advertisement Advertisement The activist questioned the lack of solidarity with the migrants. “Europe is over there,” he said. “There is plenty of space.” Frustration builds The unresolved crisis is proving to be a major challenge for Sánchez. A third of the government’s ministers have been summoned to testify in extraordinary parliamentary hearings on the situation in Ceuta, during which lawmakers belonging to political groups that have traditionally supported the prime minister are increasingly expressing their frustration with the situation in the city. Spanish National Police officers interact with a group of people in Ceuta. | Antonio Sempere Lawmaker Mikel Legarda, a member of the regionalist Basque Nationalist Party, slammed the government for “negligence” over the factors precipitating the crisis in Ceuta, and its “inaction” in returning the city to normalcy. “The question is unavoidable: Where is the state?” he asked in parliament. The Sánchez government on Tuesday unveiled a €309 million stimulus package to reinforce Ceuta’s security infrastructure, reinforce public services, aid local businesses and humanitarian support for migrants. Advertisement Advertisement “The main objective of the decree is to give confidence to both businesses and workers,” said Deputy Prime Minister and Economy Minister Carlos Cuerpo. “We are aware of the urgent need to act to restore the tranquility and confidence that Ceuta’s citizens and businesses need.” But it remains unclear whether the measures will be enough to heal the lasting rifts the crisis is creating within the exclave. Ceuta has long prided itself on being a bastion of hospitality and peaceful coexistence between Christians and Muslims on the North African coast, but the migrant influx is testing that identity, with locals like Ali Amar rejecting newcomers he said have “brought chaos” to the city.” “I am Muslim. I am Spanish. I am a patriot,” he said. “These people have no business being here.”

https://www.dw.com/en/ukraine-russian-st.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5MjRT Russia is increasingly targeting petrol stations in Kyiv [File photo] Image: Alina Smutko/REUTERS Advertisement Russian airstrikes on Ukrainian cities of Kyiv and Odesa injured at least 13 people early on Thursday, Ukrainian officials said, as the war heads toward its fifth winter. "An air raid alert has been declared in Kyiv due to the threat of missile strikes. We urge residents to proceed to the nearest shelters," the Kyiv City Military Administration wrote on Telegram. At least 10 people were wounded in the Ukrainian capital, officials said on the messaging app. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said apartment buildings and warehouses had been damaged in the latest strikes, and that debris also fell near a petrol station. News agencies such as Reuters and AFP cited witnesses hearing "strong" explosions in Kyiv. In the Black Sea port City of Odesa, at least three people were injured when a Russian strike hit a 19-story apartment building, authorities said. A child was among those injured. Both Russia and Ukraine have increased their use of long-range missiles in recent months, along with the continued use of drones, to strike inside each other's territories. Mediated talks ahead? The strikes continue even as Russia and Ukraine recently signalled their readiness to resume talks under US mediation . Earlier this week, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy's office said officials were preparing for talks in October. Similar signals came from Moscow, which said it did not rule out such a possibility. The last round of trilateral talks took place in January and February 2026 in Abu Dhabi and Geneva, without producing a breakthrough, as the issue of territory control in eastern Ukraine remained unresolved.
